standard.title: Interpret information from sources
standard.description: interpret information and data from observations and provided sources, including the comparison of objects from the past and present
standard.prior_knowledge: From Y1 (AC9HS1S03): Students used sources to answer questions and compared objects from past and present using comparative language.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students interpret information and data from observations and provided sources, including comparing objects from the past and present.

nodes.label: Interpreting distance and location on maps
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can interpret distance on maps using terms like distant, close, local, many hours, walking distance, and describe the accessibility of different features and places.
nodes.minimum_width: Interpret distance between at least two places on a map using at least two distance terms.
nodes.typical_width: Interpret geographic maps, concept maps and digital displays to explore system connections; use distance terms to decide on accessibility; interpret map symbols and legends; describe how places are connected.
wider: Interpret how First Nations Australians' songlines connect places across Country using spatial reasoning
Compare accessibility of a place by different transport modes and discuss the implications

response_modes.reason: Map distance terms require practice across different map scales and contexts before they are used fluently.

success_criteria: Uses at least two distance terms accurately when describing map locations
Interprets at least one map symbol or legend element correctly

nodes.label: Comparing objects and activities across places and time
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify how objects and activities are similar or different depending on conditions in local and distant places, and across time periods.
nodes.minimum_width: Compare at least two objects or activities across either time (past/present) or place (local/distant) and identify one similarity and one difference.
nodes.typical_width: Identify similarities and differences between clothes, transport and technology depending on conditions in local and distant places; compare past and present objects; use comparative and contextual reasoning.
wider: Compare objects and activities across all three dimensions simultaneously: place, time and cultural context
Investigate why similar needs (shelter, food, communication) have been met differently in different places and times

response_modes.reason: Comparing across both time and place is a significant cognitive step — build range through multiple comparison examples before asking students to do multi-dimensional comparisons.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: Multi-dimensional comparison (place AND time) is a powerful historical-geographical thinking skill — students who can compare across both dimensions simultaneously develop significantly richer analytical capability.
success_criteria: Compares at least two items across time or place
Identifies at least one similarity and one difference with a contextual reason
